children: Indonesia's growth could remain near its current trend rather than accelerate materially toward the finance ministry's expectation of up to 6%, RHB analysts Muhamad Farid Anas bin Johari and Wong Xian Yong say in a note. RHB maintains its 2026 GDP growth forecast at 5.2%, with stronger investment likely to offset weaker household spending, government expenditure and exports. Investment should account for a larger share of growth, supported by the continuing investment cycle and gradual rollout of Danantara-related projects. However, a broader recovery in consumption and external demand will be needed for a sustained move toward 6% growth, they say. 2026 headline inflation is forecast at 2.8%, with risks tilted slightly higher. Bank Indonesia may raise its policy rate by 25 bps to 6.0% in 4Q as it prioritizes financial stability. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)
